html:
The Umm an-Nar culture was the Bronze Age culture of what is now the UAE and northern Oman, from about 2600 to 2000 BCE. It is named after a small island next to Abu Dhabi where its remains were first dug up.

Its people built large round stone tombs for collective burial, and towers in their oases. They mined and smelted copper in the Hajar mountains and shipped it to Mesopotamia, which called the land Magan. Pottery and beads show trade with the Indus cities too.

They grew dates, wheat and barley in oases watered by wells. The culture is the oldest chapter of the UAE's own history.
